edits.say: Push the red snap wire into the very first hole at the far left end of the outer rail, the one along the red line. Push the black snap wire into the first hole at the far left of the rail just inside it, along the blue line.
placements: red snap wire → far-left end hole of the outer + rail (the row along the red line on the edge farthest from you)
black snap wire → far-left end hole of the inner − rail (the row along the blue line), directly below the red wire

why: At 0:50-0:58 and in step-1.jpg the red and black wires go into the leftmost holes of the two rails on the far edge: red in the outer row by the red line, black in the row below it by the blue line. The column is readable as the board's left end, so 'match the picture' isn't needed.

edits.say: Find the LED's long leg and short leg. Put the short leg into the blue minus rail. Put the long leg straight down into column 20, the first strip just below the blue line, about ten holes right of the battery wires.
placements: blue 5mm LED short (cathode) leg → inner − rail (along the blue line)
blue 5mm LED long (anode) leg → terminal strip column 20, top holes just below the blue line (columns are numbered downward from left, 30 to 1)

why: At 1:00-1:22 the LED goes in with one leg in the blue − rail and the other in the terminal strip. The zoomed lit frame at 2:34-2:40 (step-5.jpg) shows that leg in the column labelled 20. On this board the column numbers count down from left to right. The reading is from a slanted view, so it could be off by one.

edits.instruction: Bridge the LED's column to a new column with the short red jumper.
edits.say: Take the short red jumper with bent ends. Put its left end in column 20, the LED's column, a few holes lower down. Put its right end four columns to the right, in column 16. It lies flat, going left to right.
placements: short red jumper left end → column 20 (same strip as the LED long leg), lower in the strip
short red jumper right end → column 16, same row as the left end; jumper lies flat across columns 20→16

why: At 1:28-1:34 the jumper is laid flat, going left to right, below the LED. In the 2:36 zoom its left end is under the LED leg (col 20) and its right end is under the resistor leg (col 16). The current text puts both ends in the LED's row, which is wrong and would do nothing electrically.

edits.instruction: Bend the resistor's legs and plug it from the + rail into the jumper's right-hand column.
edits.say: Bend both resistor legs down so it stands up like a staple. Put one leg in the outer red plus rail along the red line. Put the other leg into column 16, the same column as the jumper's right end.
placements: resistor top lead → outer + rail (row along the red line), just right of the LED
resistor other lead → column 16, top of the strip just below the blue line, same column as the red jumper's right end (not the LED's column)

why: At 1:46-1:58 he bends the resistor leads. At 2:00-2:08 he plugs one lead into the outer red + rail and the other into the terminal strip at column 16, above the jumper's right end (2:36 zoom). The old text said the LED anode's row, but the resistor shares a column with the jumper, not with the LED.
At 2:18-2:24 the snap is pressed onto the 9V and the LED lights blue by 2:24. The step matches the video and the short-circuit warning is real for a 9V.
